papers.name: MEgATrack: Monochrome Egocentric Articulated Hand-Tracking for Virtual Reality
papers.venue: SIGGRAPH / ACM Transactions on Graphics (TOG), Vol. 39, No. 4, Article 87
papers.summary: MEgATrack is a real-time egocentric hand-tracking system for VR headsets that ingests 4 synchronized monochrome VGA fisheye cameras and outputs 26-DOF articulated 3D poses and rigged meshes for both hands. Per image it produces per-hand bounding boxes (via a lightweight SSD-style DetNet, or by extrapolating the previous two tracked poses), crops and feeds them to KeyNet which predicts 21 2D-location heatmaps plus 1D relative-distance heatmaps, then fits a template hand model across all views by minimizing a 2D + distance + temporal energy with Levenberg-Marquardt. Extrapolated poses feed back to seed both the detector boxes and the KeyNet keypoint-augmentation channel, giving temporally smooth, low-jitter tracking at 60Hz on PC / 30Hz on mobile.
papers.rig: 4 synchronized global-shutter monochrome VGA (640x480) fisheye cameras (150deg W x 120deg H x 175deg diag FOV) rigidly mounted on a VR headset; lower-center region seen by 2+ cameras (stereo), side regions monocular
papers.outputs: Per-hand 26-DOF articulated 3D hand pose theta (6-DOF global R,t + 4 rotational DOF per finger), 21 3D keypoints per hand, per-user global hand scale phi, and a linear-blend-skinned rigged hand mesh; also a per-hand DetNet confidence scalar

nodes.label: 4 mono VGA fisheye cameras
nodes.desc: Synchronized global-shutter 640x480 monochrome fisheye images from headset-mounted rig

nodes.label: DetNet hand detection
nodes.desc: SSD-inspired lightweight CNN regressing 2D hand center + scalar radius + presence confidence per hand (left/right); boxes are squares inscribing circles, kept when conf>0.5; at runtime run round-robin on one camera
nodes.models: DetNet (SSD/YOLO-style single-shot regressor), MSE loc loss + BCE conf loss (lambda=100)

nodes.label: Detection-by-tracking box extrapolation
nodes.desc: When a hand is tracked, extrapolate pose theta_hat_t = 2*theta_{t-1} - theta_{t-2}, project 21 keypoints into each camera, take min enclosing circle as the box; avoids running DetNet every frame and yields temporally smooth boxes
nodes.models: constant-position pose extrapolation + keypoint reprojection + min-enclosing-circle

nodes.label: Crop + keypoint-feature augmentation
nodes.desc: Crop square bbox (enlarged 20%), for right hand mirror along x; augment KeyNet input with projected extrapolated 21 keypoints (2D coord in [0,1] + 1D relative distance), zeros if untracked

nodes.label: KeyNet 2D + 1D heatmaps
nodes.desc: CNN taking a 96x96 crop plus a 63-dim extrapolated-keypoint vector; outputs 21x18x18 2D Gaussian location heatmaps and 21x18 1D relative-distance heatmaps, promoting spatial + temporal consistency
nodes.models: KeyNet (heatmap regressor, Tompson-style Gaussian targets), MSE on 2D+1D heatmaps (alpha=0.05)

nodes.label: 21 keypoints + relative distance
nodes.desc: Per-view 2D image keypoints p_hat_{i,j} and 1D relative distance d_rel = (d_i - mean_d)/phi; distance chosen over depth to remove fisheye crop ambiguity

nodes.label: Model-based pose fit min E(theta)
nodes.desc: Fit 26-DOF template hand by minimizing E_2D (reprojection) + w1*E_dist (relative distance) + w2*E_temporal (||theta - theta_{t-1}||^2); aggregates all 4 views; LM solver initialized from previous frame or neutral pose
nodes.models: template hand model (kinematic skeleton S + LBS mesh M), Levenberg-Marquardt, w1=0.04 w2=20

nodes.label: Hand scale calibration (phi)
nodes.desc: Resolves size/distance ambiguity by jointly optimizing pose + shared global scale phi over multiple frames where a hand is in the stereo region; block-diagonal Jacobian gives O(n) LM step; ~5s per new user
nodes.models: multi-frame LM, shared scale parameter phi

nodes.label: 3D hand pose + rigged mesh
nodes.desc: Final per-hand articulated pose, 3D keypoints, and LBS-rigged mesh sent to the VR renderer

papers.posekit_notes: DetNet maps to posekit 'detect' (single-shot box regressor with confidence). Detection-by-tracking is consumer glue (temporal box propagation) with no direct posekit role - closest is 'track'/'temporal'. KeyNet maps to posekit 'pose2d' (2D heatmap keypoint estimator), but its extra 1D relative-distance head is non-standard and the extrapolated-keypoint input channel is consumer glue. The min E(theta) stage maps to 'fit-model' + 'triangulate'/'optimize' (LM fit of a template skeleton against multi-view reprojection). Hand scale calibration maps to 'calibrate' (per-user shape). The temporal prior (theta_{t-1}) and pose extrapolation are 'temporal' glue. Final LBS mesh + rigged output is consumer rendering glue beyond posekit's keypoint scope.

papers.name: UmeTrack: Unified multi-view end-to-end hand tracking for VR
papers.summary: UmeTrack is a single end-to-end differentiable network that tracks hands from VR-headset egocentric wide-FOV cameras and directly regresses the articulated skeleton pose (20 joint angles plus a 6DoF wrist/root transform) in world space, rather than root-relative 3D keypoints. Per-hand perspective crops from one or more views are encoded, lifted to a shared reference-camera 3D frame via FTL, fused across views (learnable feature-space triangulation), temporally smoothed by a recurrent module, concatenated with a skeleton-encoder feature, and decoded by a regressor whose predicted root sample points are turned into a 6DoF root pose via SVD; forward kinematics then combines joint angles + root + skeleton to output absolute 3D hand pose. For unknown users, Regressor-U additionally calibrates hand scale from multi-view data.
papers.rig: Single- or multi-view egocentric wide-FOV fisheye monochrome (or RGB) cameras mounted on a VR headset (dataset uses 4 VGA monochrome cameras; a hand appears in 1 or 2 views); per-hand perspective crops with known virtual-camera intrinsics/extrinsics, ROI provided per frame
papers.outputs: Per-frame articulated hand pose: 20 joint angles theta and wrist/root 6DoF transform T_H in world coordinates (known-skeleton output {theta, T_H}); unknown-user path (Regressor-U) additionally outputs calibrated hand scale/skeleton H-hat ({theta, T_H, H}). Forward kinematics + linear blend skinning produce the absolute 3D keypoints/hand mesh.

nodes.label: Perspective cropping
nodes.desc: Given a hand ROI, creates a virtual perspective camera at the original camera location with z-axis pointing at the ROI center; warps the fisheye image to a distortion-corrected crop with known virtual intrinsics K_i and extrinsics T_i,1. At train time intrinsics are set so all GT keypoints project inside the crop; at inference intrinsics are estimated from the previously tracked pose.
nodes.models: virtual perspective camera + image warping (Remelli 2020 / Yu 2021)

nodes.label: CNN encoder (shared)
nodes.desc: Fully-convolutional (ResNet-based, 96x96 monochrome input) encoder applied per view with shared weights, producing image-space latent features z_i^I without camera geometry.
nodes.models: fully-convolutional ResNet encoder, weight-shared across views

nodes.label: FTL 3D lift
nodes.desc: Feature Transform Layer: z_i^3d = FTL(z_i^I | T_i,1 * K_i^-1). Unprojects image features with virtual intrinsics K_i^-1 and transforms from virtual camera i into the reference-camera (camera 1) 3D frame via T_i,1, yielding camera-geometry-aware features all in the same 3D space.

nodes.label: Multi-view fusion
nodes.desc: Concatenates per-view z_i^3d and fuses them (1x1-conv residual blocks) into a single z^3d of identical shape, performing learnable feature-space triangulation; bypassed (z^3d = z_1^3d) for single-view input. Key to hand-scale prediction.
nodes.models: MVF fusion module (learnable triangulation, Iskakov 2019; 1x1 conv residual blocks)

nodes.label: Temporal module (RNN)
nodes.desc: Recurrent network with hidden state h_TEM that fuses z^3d with temporal context to produce z^TEM = TEM(z^3d, h_TEM); provides temporal consistency and robustness under severe occlusion.
nodes.models: recurrent neural network (1x1 conv + ReLU; hidden state carried across frames)

nodes.label: Skeleton encoder
nodes.desc: Featurizes a known hand skeleton H (20 joints x 6D rest joint positions + rotation axes = 120-D vector) into feature maps z^H = SE(H), injecting per-user hand geometry prior.

nodes.label: Concat
nodes.desc: Concatenates temporal features z^TEM with skeleton features z^H into z^R carrying 3D, temporal and skeleton information: z^R = concat(z^TEM, z^H).

nodes.label: Regressor-K / Regressor-U
nodes.desc: Takes z^R and predicts 20 joint angles theta-hat and root sample points v-hat (21-D = 7 points x 3) in reference-camera space. Regressor-U (unknown skeleton, requires multi-view z^TEM) additionally predicts a 1-D hand scale to build calibrated skeleton H-hat; the model dynamically selects the regressor at inference by skeleton availability.
nodes.models: Regressor-K (known skeleton), Regressor-U (unknown skeleton, scale calib); residual blocks x2 + pool

nodes.label: SVD root fit
nodes.desc: Aligns 7 pre-defined local root sample points v_H to the predicted points v-hat via SVD (least-squares rigid motion) to decode the wrist/root 6DoF transform T_H,1 in reference-camera space, then maps to world using reference-camera extrinsics.

nodes.label: Forward kinematics
nodes.desc: Combines joint angles theta, decoded 6DoF root pose T_H and skeleton H via forward kinematics (+ linear blend skinning) to output absolute 3D hand pose (keypoints/mesh) for VR rendering and interaction.
nodes.models: forward kinematics on hand skeleton + LBS

nodes.label: VR hand pose
nodes.desc: Final absolute 3D hand pose (world-space keypoints/mesh) consumed by VR rendering and interaction (e.g. pinch detection).

papers.figure_caption: Fig. 2 (UmeTrack): End-to-end architecture for the known-hand-skeleton case. Left "3D feature extractor" runs per view: perspective crops I_1 (and optional I_2) go through a weight-shared CNN encoder, an FTL layer that lifts image features to the shared reference-camera 3D frame, and a multi-view fusion module producing z^3d. Right "Pose regression": a recurrent temporal module (self-loop) yields z^TEM, concatenated with skeleton-encoder features z^H into z^R; Regressor-K predicts joint angles and root sample points, an SVD block decodes the 6DoF root pose, and forward kinematics combines angles + root + skeleton into the final hand pose. Legend distinguishes multi-view vs single-view dataflow, input/output data, trainable vs non-trainable modules, and feature maps.
traits: temporal feedback loop (recurrent hidden state h_TEM across frames)
previous-pose feedback drives ROI selection and virtual-camera intrinsics at inference
learnable feature-space triangulation via FTL + multi-view fusion
view-count-agnostic: single-view and multi-view share one network (MVF bypassed for n=1)

absolute world-space 3D root pose enabling acceleration/temporal loss
per-user template model: skeleton encoder injects known hand geometry (120-D skeleton feature)
online hand-scale self-calibration for unknown users (Regressor-U, multi-view only)
SVD rigid alignment decodes 6DoF root from 7 predicted sample points
forward-kinematics + LBS to produce final absolute pose

swappable known/unknown-skeleton regressor selected dynamically at inference
papers.posekit_notes: Roles that map to posekit-style stages: crop/rewarp (perspective cropping with virtual camera), pose2d (per-view CNN encoder producing image features), lift3d (FTL), triangulate (multi-view fusion / learnable feature-space triangulation), temporal (RNN temporal module), identity/template (skeleton encoder = per-user hand template), fit-model (Regressor + forward kinematics = skeleton fitting/decode), optimize (SVD root-pose decode via least-squares rigid motion). Consumer glue specific to UmeTrack: the feedback edge from forward-kinematics back to perspective cropping (uses tracked pose t-1 to set ROI and estimate virtual intrinsics) and the dynamic Regressor-K vs Regressor-U switch based on whether a hand skeleton is provided. No explicit detector/segment stage is shown in Fig. 2 (ROI is assumed / fed by the tracking loop). The 'pose2d' role is a loose fit: the encoder emits latent feature maps, not explicit 2D keypoints.

papers.name: Kineo: Calibration-Free Metric Motion Capture From Sparse RGB Cameras
papers.summary: Kineo is a fully automatic, calibration-free and synchronization-free pipeline for markerless multi-view motion capture from sparse consumer RGB cameras. It audio-syncs the streams, feeds 2D keypoints from a swappable off-the-shelf detector into a graph-based auto-calibration (essential-matrix edges, loop-closure relative scales, MST initialization, three-pass bundle adjustment that also fits Brown-Conrady distortion), then weighted-DLT triangulates the skeleton and estimates scene pointmaps, and finally recovers metric scale via an SMPL body prior or the MoGe monocular metric-depth estimator. Every geometric stage is driven by the 2D detector confidences, and each triangulated 3D keypoint gets a pairwise-reprojection consensus confidence score.
papers.rig: Sparse set of N uncalibrated, unsynchronized, battery-powered consumer RGB cameras (static cameras, moving subject), each with an audio track; no markers, no hardware sync, no manual calibration. Cross-view subject re-identification is assumed given (Sec. 8 implementation details).
papers.outputs: Metric-scale scene: 3D keypoints (COCO-19 / COCO-133 / Human3.6M skeletons or full parametric SMPL body) with per-point pairwise-reprojection confidence, dense scene pointmaps, and complete camera parameters (extrinsics, intrinsics/focal, Brown-Conrady distortion coefficients).

nodes.label: Unsynced uncalibrated RGB views (View 1..N + audio)
nodes.desc: Sparse consumer cameras, static rig, moving subject; each has an audio track. Cross-view subject re-ID assumed given.

nodes.label: Audio Temporal Sync (Sec.4)
nodes.desc: Estimates per-camera temporal lag by MFCC cross-correlation against a reference camera, aligning detections on a shared global timeline; derives subframe-accuracy conditions from hop length and inter-mic distances.

nodes.label: 2D Keypoint Detection (swappable)
nodes.desc: Off-the-shelf 2D keypoint detector run per synchronized view, producing 2D keypoints x_{i,k} with per-keypoint confidence w_{i,k} in [0,1]. Detector is replaceable without changing the architecture; extended MMPose for GPU-resident batched inference.

nodes.label: Confidence-Aware Spatio-Temporal Keypoint Sampling (Sec.5.2.1)
nodes.desc: Scores each correspondence by geometric mean of detector confidences w_ij,k=sqrt(w_i,k*w_j,k); keeps only w>tau, then randomly selects M correspondences to implicitly promote temporal diversity and geometric coverage. Fixed compute cost for scalability.

nodes.label: Pairwise SfM / Essential-Matrix Graph (Sec.5.1-5.3)
nodes.desc: Builds a camera graph: nodes=cameras, edges=pairwise essential matrix E_ij (rotation R_ij + translation direction t_ij) via 5-point + RANSAC on sampled correspondences. Intrinsics initialized from MoGe (later reused for pointmaps). Edge weight = average Sampson distance over inliers (calibration reliability).
nodes.models: five-point algorithm + RANSAC; MoGe intrinsics init; Sampson distance

nodes.label: Loop-Closure Relative Scales (Sec.5.4)
nodes.desc: Recovers per-edge relative scales lambda_ij from triplet loop-closure constraints WA*lambda=0, weighted by loop score (geo-mean of edge reliabilities). Solved as regularized weighted nonlinear least-squares with a ||lambda-1|| term via L-BFGS in log-space.

nodes.label: MST Absolute Extrinsics (Sec.5.5)
nodes.desc: Kruskal MST over the camera graph (edge weights = calibration reliability); composes relative [R|t]_ij with lambda_ij along the optimal path from origin camera C0 to each camera to get globally consistent absolute extrinsics with minimal error accumulation.

nodes.label: 3-Pass Bundle Adjustment (Sec.5.6)
nodes.desc: Refines cameras on a confident 2-view-visible keypoint subset: pass1 extrinsics+3D points, pass2 +focal lengths, pass3 +Brown-Conrady distortion. Minimizes confidence-weighted Huber reprojection loss (weights = 2D detector confidence).
nodes.models: iterative BA, Huber loss, Brown-Conrady distortion model

nodes.label: Undistort (images + 2D keypoints)
nodes.desc: Applies the estimated Brown-Conrady distortion coefficients to undistort images (for pointmaps) and 2D keypoints (before triangulation).

nodes.label: Weighted-DLT Triangulation + Confidence (Sec.6.2-6.3)
nodes.desc: Lifts undistorted 2D keypoints to 3D across all N views via confidence-weighted DLT (weight = 2D confidence w_i,m). Assigns each 3D point a pairwise-reprojection consensus score s_m from focal-normalized reprojection residuals mapped through exp(-lambda*residual) and averaged over view pairs.

nodes.label: Scene Pointmaps (Sec.6.1)
nodes.desc: Dense scene geometry from undistorted images: MoGe (per-view metric pointmap merged via extrinsics, given estimated focal) or VGGT (multi-view, aligned to Kineo cameras via similarity transform).

nodes.label: Metric-Scale Recovery (Sec.7)
nodes.desc: Recovers global scale alpha: (a) SMPL body prior - optimize scale alpha + shape beta to match bone lengths of the arbitrary-unit skeleton (pose ignored, no LBS), confidence-weighted Huber; or (b) subject-agnostic route using the MoGe monocular metric-depth estimator (scale = metric/arbitrary joint-depth ratio). Fitting SMPL uses NLF surface keypoints + NLF SMPLFitter.
nodes.models: SMPL (M(beta), regressor J), NLF SMPLFitter; MoGe monocular metric depth

nodes.label: Metric-scale scene (3D keypoints+conf, pointmaps, cameras)
nodes.desc: Final metric outputs: 3D skeletons or SMPL body with per-point confidence, dense pointmaps, and full camera intrinsics/extrinsics/distortion; alpha rescales skeletons, pointmaps and cameras.

papers.figure_caption: Figure 1: Overview of the Kineo pipeline for markerless motion capture from uncalibrated and unsynchronized multi-camera videos. Raw videos are first audio-synchronized to a shared timeline; a swappable 2D keypoint detector produces per-view keypoints with confidence; automatic camera calibration builds an essential-matrix graph (confidence-aware sampling, SfM, MST) and refines cameras + Brown-Conrady distortion via three-pass bundle adjustment; images/keypoints are undistorted, then weighted-DLT triangulation and MoGe/VGGT pointmaps yield an arbitrary-scale scene with per-point confidence; finally metric-scale recovery (SMPL body prior or MoGe monocular metric depth) produces the metric-scale scene.

confidence-driven correspondence sampling for calibration

papers.posekit_notes: Maps cleanly onto posekit roles: 2D Keypoint Detection = posekit pose2d runtime (the detector is explicitly swappable - NLF/RTMPose/DWPose - matching posekit's runtime abstraction). Triangulation = a lift3d/triangulate role (weighted DLT), and the pairwise-reprojection confidence is a posekit-style per-keypoint confidence carried through. Camera calibration (SfM essential-matrix graph, loop-closure scales, MST, bundle adjustment with Brown-Conrady) is consumer glue outside posekit's keypoint scope - it is a classical geometric calibrate/optimize block. Scene pointmaps (MoGe/VGGT) and metric-scale recovery (SMPL fit via NLF SMPLFitter, or MoGe monocular metric depth) are fit-model / other consumer stages. Audio temporal sync and GPU decode are pre-processing glue with no posekit equivalent.

papers.name: EPFL-Smart-Kitchen-30: Automatic 3D Body/Hand Motion Estimation (annotation pipeline)
papers.summary: An offline annotation pipeline that turns a synchronized multi-view (9 static RGB-D Kinect cameras) plus egocentric (HoloLens 2) capture of cooking behavior into ground-truth 3D full-body + hand motion. It runs four stages: per-view RTMPose 2D keypoint estimation, Kinect-SDK identity tracking (3D merge + reproject-to-select) to disambiguate the subject across views, confidence-based SVD triangulation to lift 3D keypoints, and EasyMocap multi-view SMPL/MANO mesh fitting that also fuses HoloLens 2 egocentric hand poses. The output is per-frame SMPL body and MANO hand parameters, with a discard-frame verification step against the lifted pose.
papers.rig: 9 static Azure Kinect RGB-D cameras (30 FPS) at strategic points in the kitchen (ceiling, wall corners, near sink) providing multi-view RGB + depth, plus one head-mounted HoloLens 2 egocentric device (RGB + depth + hand tracking + eye gaze), and wireless IMUs (100 FPS). Calibrated with an A0-size checkerboard; poses expressed in a global world coordinate system.
papers.outputs: Per-frame 3D full-body pose as fitted SMPL parameters (pose, shape, global transform) and 3D hand pose as fitted MANO parameters; equivalently reprojected/triangulated 3D keypoints in the COCO joint layout. Low-confidence joints (score < 0.1) are excluded from fitting and fitting-artifact frames are dropped.

nodes.label: Multi-view RGBD video (9 Kinect cams)
nodes.desc: Synchronized 30 FPS exocentric RGB-D video from the calibrated static camera rig; per-view input to 2D pose and to Kinect body tracking.

nodes.label: Kinect depth + body tracking
nodes.desc: Kinect Body Tracking SDK estimates per-view 3D body pose and a tracking identity from the depth images; used to fix the subject identity when experimentalists enter the scene.

nodes.label: HoloLens 2 egocentric hand estimator
nodes.desc: Egocentric depth-based hand tracking toolkit giving relative 3D hand poses with contact cues that RGB views lack.

nodes.label: RTMPose 2D keypoint estimation
nodes.desc: Per-view 2D body keypoints via RTMPose-x (8 datasets); whole-body RTMW-x (14 datasets) recovers hand keypoints using body semantic context. Emits keypoints + per-joint confidence.

nodes.label: Identity tracking / tracklet indexing
nodes.desc: Transforms Kinect per-view 3D poses to the world frame and merges them, selects the dominant identity as the subject, then reprojects that 3D pose into each view to select the correct RTMPose 2D pose (merged 3D not used as final output because it is jittery).

nodes.label: Confidence-based 3D keypoint lifting
nodes.desc: Groups the identity-selected 2D poses across all views and lifts to 3D via SVD weighted by per-view confidence scores; joints below confidence 0.1 are excluded from fitting.

nodes.label: SMPL body mesh fitting
nodes.desc: EasyMocap multi-view fit of SMPL (COCO-adapted joint regressor) to lifted 3D + RTMPose 2D, minimizing 3D joint, 2D reprojection, temporal smoothing, and regularization losses over pose/shape/global transform.

papers.name: AssemblyHands
papers.summary: AssemblyHands builds a large-scale egocentric 3D hand-pose dataset by automatically annotating multi-view exocentric RGB frames with a volumetric fusion network (MVExoNet) trained from a small set of manually-triangulated labels. MVExoNet encodes each exocentric view with EfficientNet, unprojects the 2D features into a shared 3D feature volume via softmax-weighted fusion, refines it with a V2V-PoseNet 3D CNN, and reads out 3D joints via soft-argmax, using an inference-time iterative-refinement loop that re-crops and re-roots inputs from the previous round's prediction. The resulting 3D annotations are projected into the monochrome egocentric views to train a single-view egocentric estimator (SVEgoNet), which is then evaluated via a verb/action-classification task.

papers.name: AssemblyHands-X (AssemblyX): Modeling 3D Hand-Body Coordination for Understanding Bimanual Human Activities
papers.summary: AssemblyHands-X builds a markerless 3D hand-body benchmark by annotating synchronized multi-view Assembly101 videos. Its offline annotation pipeline runs two parallel per-region branches (body and hands): each does 2D keypoint detection then confidence-weighted multi-view triangulation, the 3D joints are merged into a unified upper-body+hands skeleton, and finally SMPL-X parameters are fit per frame by minimizing a 3D-joint loss plus a differentiable silhouette loss against SAM human masks. The output is per-frame 3D hand-body keypoints and SMPL-X mesh parameters used downstream for action recognition.

papers.name: MAMMA: Markerless Accurate Multi-person Motion Acquisition
papers.summary: MAMMA is an offline markerless multi-view motion-capture pipeline that recovers per-frame SMPL-X bodies for one or two closely-interacting people from synchronized calibrated RGB videos. Each view is segmented and tracked with SAM2, a novel transformer dense-landmark network (MammaNet) predicts N=512 surface landmarks with per-landmark uncertainty, visibility and contact conditioned on the mask, and a robust multi-stage LBFGS optimizer fits SMPL-X to the confidence-weighted, cross-view-matched landmarks. It aims to match commercial marker-based (Vicon) accuracy without manual cleanup.

papers.summary: A multi-stage offline annotation pipeline that produces accurate 3D hand-pose ground truth from a mobile backpack rig of 8 exocentric fisheye cameras plus 2 egocentric Meta Quest 3 fisheye cameras (10 views total), all hardware-synchronized and MoCap-calibrated into a shared moving reference frame. Per view it runs a Sapiens body keypoint detector to get 42 hand keypoints (21 per hand) and localize hands, then perspective-crops each hand into a virtual pinhole 256x256 image (with histogram equalization) and runs the InterNet hand-specific detector for a second independent set of 2D keypoints. Confidence-filtered 2D detections (threshold 0.3) from both models across all 10 views are RANSAC-triangulated into 42 3D keypoints, to which a personalized LBS hand mesh is fit via inverse kinematics and projected back to the 2D views for the final overlay.

papers.name: HO-Cap: A Capture System and Dataset for 3D Reconstruction and Pose Tracking of Hand-Object Interaction
papers.summary: HO-Cap is a semi-automatic offline annotation pipeline that turns synchronized multi-view RGB-D videos of hand-object interaction into 3D shape and 6-DoF pose annotations for hands (MANO) and objects. Per frame it runs two parallel branches — object masks (SAM2) + FoundationPose 6D tracking with cross-view RANSAC consistency and SDF refinement, and MediaPipe 2D hand joints triangulated with RANSAC into MANO fits — then a joint hand-object SDF optimization resolves interpenetration, followed by render-back to all camera views for verification and 2D annotation export.
papers.rig: 8 statically-mounted, extrinsically-calibrated Intel RealSense D455 RGB-D cameras positioned above a table (world frame near table center), plus one higher-resolution Microsoft Azure Kinect (also above the table, used primarily for per-object 3D reconstruction) and a Microsoft HoloLens headset for egocentric capture. Calibrated with Vicalib. For per-object reconstruction the object is manually moved in front of the Azure Kinect and a textured mesh is built offline with BundleSDF (LoFTR matching + marching cubes).
papers.outputs: Per-frame 6-DoF object poses T=(R,t) in SE(3) in the world frame for each object; MANO hand pose params theta (R^51) and pre-calibrated shape beta (R^10) for 1-2 hands; reconstructed 64 textured 3D object meshes; 3D hand/object meshes projected back to each camera view as 2D image annotations; refined HoloLens poses.

nodes.label: FoundationPose per-view 6D tracking

nodes.label: Cross-view pose consistency + RANSAC

nodes.label: MediaPipe 2D hand joints + filtering

nodes.label: Triangulation + RANSAC 3D keypoints

nodes.label: Joint hand-object SDF optimization
nodes.desc: Jointly refines all object poses and MANO hand poses using object+hand SDFs on fused segmented point clouds plus regularization and temporal smoothness; reduces hand-object mesh interpenetration. Hand masks/points from SAM2 prompted by keypoint bbox+2D joints, isolated via point-to-mesh threshold

nodes.label: Final hand-object pose (world frame)

nodes.label: Render to camera views
nodes.desc: Projects the refined 3D hand+object shapes into every camera view to verify alignment and export 2D image annotations

canonical_stages.name: Capture / calibration
canonical_stages.desc: The synchronized multi-view (and/or ego+exo) image source plus the camera model. Covers the physical rig, hardware or audio sync, and intrinsics/extrinsics — whether assumed-given (MAMMA, EPFL, AssemblyX, HO-Cap), MoCap-registered into a moving frame (EgoExo-Hands), or solved downstream from the keypoints themselves (Kineo's calibration-free auto-calibration is deferred to the association/calibrate stage). Optional for single-headset realtime rigs where geometry is fixed by construction (MEgATrack/UmeTrack).
canonical_stages.boundary_type: Synchronized per-(view,frame) images + CameraModel (intrinsics/extrinsics, possibly unknown)

canonical_stages.name: Detect / segment / localize instance
canonical_stages.desc: First localization of the instance(s): a box detector (MEgATrack DetNet, AssemblyHands body-keypoint detector), a promptable/video segmenter producing masks (MAMMA SAM2, AssemblyX SAM, HO-Cap SAM2), a full-frame dense-skeleton net that doubles as the localizer (EgoExo-Hands Sapiens, Kineo/EPFL/AssemblyX's whole-body 2D detectors), or nothing at all when an ROI is supplied by the tracking loop (UmeTrack). Produces the region/mask that conditions the 2D estimator. Masks are first-class here for MAMMA/AssemblyX/HO-Cap (model inputs or fitting targets), not just visualization.
canonical_stages.boundary_type: BoxDetections (boxes + optional masks + optional track_ids) or per-instance ROI

canonical_stages.name: Cross-view / temporal identity association
canonical_stages.desc: Assigns a consistent instance id across views and/or across frames so downstream triangulation and fitting operate on the right person/hand. Realized as epipolar-affinity + Hungarian + cycle-consistent graph (MAMMA), Kinect-depth 3D-merge + reproject-to-select (EPFL), body-skeleton-fixed hand identity (AssemblyHands), left/right hand-identity head (AssemblyHands SVEgoNet). Absent / assumed-given for single-instance or externally-re-ID'd pipelines (Kineo assumes re-ID given; MEgATrack/UmeTrack fix hands by rig side; AssemblyX/EgoExo-Hands/HO-Cap are single/fixed-instance).
canonical_stages.boundary_type: instance_id per (view, frame) detection; cross-view correspondence graph

canonical_stages.name: Crop / rewarp to canonical view
canonical_stages.desc: Warps each localized instance into the canonical input space of the 2D estimator: square box crop with padding + left/right mirror (MEgATrack), fisheye->virtual-pinhole perspective crop (UmeTrack, EgoExo-Hands, AssemblyHands ego), body/hand region crop (AssemblyX), undistortion of images + 2D keypoints (Kineo). Also the site of extra input channels (MEgATrack's projected-keypoint augmentation) and preprocessing (EgoExo-Hands histogram equalization). This is the universal currency between localization and 2D estimation.
canonical_stages.boundary_type: per-instance canonical crop + virtual CameraModel (K, extrinsics to reference)

canonical_stages.name: 2D keypoint / dense-landmark / feature estimation
canonical_stages.desc: The swappable per-view estimator: a top-down 2D keypoint net (MEgATrack KeyNet heatmaps, Kineo NLF/RTMPose/DWPose, EPFL RTMPose-x/RTMW-x, AssemblyX DWPose, EgoExo-Hands Sapiens+InterNet, HO-Cap MediaPipe), a dense-landmark net with uncertainty/visibility/contact (MAMMA MammaNet 512 pts), or a latent image feature encoder that never emits explicit keypoints (UmeTrack CNN encoder, AssemblyHands EfficientNet). Confidence is emitted here and is load-bearing everywhere downstream (except MediaPipe, which lacks it, forcing HO-Cap to recover it via reprojection error).
canonical_stages.boundary_type: Keypoints2d = per-(view,frame,instance) (x, y, confidence) in a named skeleton (+ optional uncertainty/visibility/dense-landmark features)

canonical_stages.name: Triangulate / lift to 3D
canonical_stages.desc: Fuses per-view 2D estimates into 3D. Classical multi-view: confidence-weighted DLT/SVD (Kineo, EPFL, AssemblyX, HO-Cap), RANSAC triangulation (EgoExo-Hands, HO-Cap), ray-intersection init (MAMMA), 2D+triangulation of body then virtual-hand-box projection (AssemblyHands). commonalities: The universal boundary datatype is per-(view,frame,instance) keypoints as (x, y, confidence) in a named skeleton convention plus a camera model. Every pipeline (except HO-Cap's confidence-less MediaPipe, which then re-derives an equivalent weight from reprojection error) carries a scalar confidence per keypoint, and it is load-bearing at every downstream stage.

Confidence-weighted everything: triangulation weights (Kineo weighted-DLT, EPFL/AssemblyX confidence-weighted SVD/DLT, MAMMA visibility*uncertainty), detection gating (MEgATrack conf>0.5), joint dropping (EPFL conf<0.1, EgoExo-Hands thr 0.3, AssemblyX tau=0.15), calibration weights (Kineo Huber-weighted BA + Sampson edge weights), and robust fit weights (MAMMA Geman-McClure). Where confidence is missing it is manufactured (HO-Cap reprojection-error selection).

Crops / rewarps are the universal currency between localization and 2D estimation: square+pad box crops (MEgATrack), fisheye->virtual-pinhole perspective crops (UmeTrack, EgoExo-Hands, AssemblyHands ego), body/hand region crops (AssemblyX), and undistortion of images+keypoints (Kineo). The 2D estimator always sees a canonicalized instance-centered view, not the raw frame.

The 2D estimator is a swappable slot: MEgATrack KeyNet, Kineo (NLF/RTMPose/DWPose explicitly swappable), EPFL (RTMPose-x/RTMW-x), AssemblyX (DWPose), EgoExo-Hands (Sapiens+InterNet), HO-Cap (MediaPipe). Matches the design doc's 'frames->posed instances' swap point; detector/tracker/pose are independently mix-and-matchable.

The tail is always fuse-then-fit: some 3D fusion (classical or learnable triangulation) followed by fitting a parametric/kinematic model (SMPL/SMPL-X/MANO/template-hand/LBS). 7 of 9 emit a parametric model fit; the model injects a per-user shape/skeleton prior in most (MEgATrack phi, UmeTrack skeleton encoder, EPFL/HO-Cap per-subject beta, EgoExo-Hands personalized LBS).

Temporal information is used by nearly all: realtime trackers close an explicit feedback loop (MEgATrack pose extrapolation -> boxes+KeyNet; UmeTrack RNN + ROI; HO-Cap reprojected pose -> next-frame init), while offline pipelines apply feed-forward temporal terms (MAMMA accel + mask propagation; EPFL/AssemblyX smoothing/median; Kineo audio sync; HO-Cap spline gap-fill). Only EgoExo-Hands is strictly per-frame.

The detector/localizer role is interface-not-implementation: it is variously a box detector (MEgATrack DetNet), a segmenter (MAMMA/AssemblyX/HO-Cap SAM/SAM2), a body-keypoint net that localizes hands via centroid (AssemblyHands, EgoExo-Hands Sapiens), or the tracking loop supplying the ROI (UmeTrack) — exactly the design doc's claim that PersonDetector must be satisfiable by pose-net adapters and segmenters alike.

Triangulation, cross-view association, calibration/BA, and model fitting are treated as consumer 'geometry glue' rather than the network — the swappable networks are detect/segment/2D-estimate, and each paper hand-rolls a different geometric tail (weighted DLT vs RANSAC vs ray-intersection vs learnable feature-volume vs SDF).
divergences: End-to-end learned fusion vs modular geometric tail: UmeTrack (FTL + learnable multi-view fusion + regressor + FK, one differentiable net) and AssemblyHands MVExoNet (softmax feature-volume + V2V + soft-argmax) LEARN the 3D lift, whereas Kineo/EPFL/AssemblyX/EgoExo-Hands/HO-Cap/MAMMA use classical geometry (weighted DLT, RANSAC, ray-intersection) with explicit optimizers. MEgATrack skips explicit triangulation entirely, recovering 3D only inside the model-fit energy.

Sparse joints vs dense surface landmarks: MAMMA predicts 512 dense surface landmarks with per-point uncertainty/visibility/contact from a transformer with learnable queries; everyone else predicts sparse skeletons (21/42 hand joints, COCO/whole-body body joints). This changes the fit contract (surface-point robust fit vs joint-matching fit).

Masks-as-inputs vs masks-as-targets vs no-masks: MAMMA and HO-Cap feed SAM/SAM2 masks INTO the estimator/point-cloud (first-class model inputs); AssemblyX uses SAM masks only as a silhouette optimization TARGET (render-back loss); the rest use no segmentation at all (box crops or full-frame).

Calibration-free vs calibration-given: Kineo is the sole fully calibration-free + sync-free pipeline (audio sync + keypoint-driven essential-matrix graph + MST + 3-pass BA solving extrinsics/intrinsics/distortion + metric scale). Every other pipeline assumes calibration given (checkerboard, Vicalib, MoCap marker-tree, or fixed VR rig).

Realtime closed-loop tracking vs offline batch annotation: MEgATrack/UmeTrack are realtime (30-60Hz) with pose-extrapolation feedback driving detection; the rest are offline annotation/capture pipelines. This splits the temporal role into 'feedback loop that changes earlier stages' (MEgATrack, UmeTrack, HO-Cap object branch) vs 'feed-forward smoothing/interpolation term' (MAMMA, EPFL, AssemblyX, Kineo).

Cross-view identity solved vs assumed: MAMMA solves it internally (epipolar affinity + Hungarian + cycle-consistency), EPFL uses depth-based Kinect identity + reproject-to-select, HO-Cap uses SAM2 per-object tracking, whereas Kineo explicitly assumes re-ID given and the VR/hand pipelines fix identity by rig geometry (L/R hand by side). Multi-person is only genuinely handled by MAMMA (1-2 interacting) and, per-object, HO-Cap.

Regress-the-model vs fit-the-model: UmeTrack directly regresses articulated skeleton params (joint angles + 6DoF root via SVD) and AssemblyHands SVEgoNet regresses ego 3D joints, replacing an optimizer with a learned network; the rest run explicit iterative optimizers (LM, LBFGS, EasyMocap gradient, IK, SDF).

Metric scale recovery is a real fork only for Kineo (SMPL bone-length prior vs MoGe monocular metric depth) and a per-user scale for the VR trackers (MEgATrack phi, UmeTrack Regressor-U); calibrated multi-view pipelines get metric scale for free from known extrinsics.

Multi-modal fusion vs pure RGB: EPFL (RGB + Kinect depth + HoloLens ego hand + IMU), HO-Cap (RGB-D + depth point clouds + HoloLens), and EgoExo-Hands (ego + exo + MoCap) fuse extra modalities; Kineo/AssemblyX/AssemblyHands/MAMMA are pure RGB (MAMMA + the VR trackers add only masks/mono-fisheye).

Hand-object joint modeling: only HO-Cap couples a separate 6-DoF object-pose branch (SAM2 + FoundationPose + SDF) with the hand branch via a joint hand-object SDF optimization resolving interpenetration; all others model only bodies and/or hands.

I have everything I need. The design.md was based on a 5-paper subset (mv-api, mamma, Kineo, AssemblyHands-X, EgoExo-Hands); the survey covers 9 papers including 4 the design never saw (MEgATrack, UmeTrack, AssemblyX, HO-Cap). I'll write the proposal.

# posekit abstraction proposal — grounded in a 9-paper pipeline survey

## 1. VERDICT

**The survey confirms design.md's core thesis and its role taxonomy holds up — with four concrete amendments, all in the "geometry tail," none touching the network-role set.**

design.md's central claims are all independently reproduced by the 9-paper survey:

- **"Every pipeline is `frames → detect → (track/segment) → 2D keypoints → [associate/triangulate] → [3D/fit]`"** — the survey's `universal_mermaid` is this exact chain plus the feedback edges design.md's realtime discussion already anticipated. Confirmed.
- **"The universal boundary datatype is per-`(view,frame,instance)` `(x, y, confidence)` in a named skeleton + camera model, and confidence is load-bearing everywhere"** — this is the survey's #1 commonality verbatim, and its strongest finding (HO-Cap's confidence-less MediaPipe *manufactures* an equivalent weight from reprojection error, proving confidence is structurally required). Confirmed and strengthened.
- **"The 2D estimator is a swappable slot; detector/tracker/pose are independently mix-and-matchable"** — survey commonality #4, across all 9. Confirmed.
- **"`PersonDetector` must be an interface satisfiable by box detectors, segmenters, and pose-net adapters alike"** — survey commonality #7 enumerates exactly these four localizer shapes (box net / segmenter / pose-as-detector / ROI-from-loop). Confirmed.
- **"Triangulation, association, calibration/BA, fitting, scale are consumer geometry glue, not networks"** — survey commonality #8 / divergence on classical-vs-learned tail. Mostly confirmed (see amendment 4).
- **The four inference paradigms (top-down / bottom-up / one-stage / query-based)** — the four newly-surveyed papers add no fifth paradigm. MEgATrack KeyNet and EgoExo-Hands are top-down; UmeTrack/AssemblyHands feature-encoders are top-down-style latent nets. Confirmed.

**Amendments needed** (the 4 new papers stress the design where the original 5 did not):

1. **The `crop` / rewarp stage must be promoted to a first-class, camera-model-aware node — not a "later" bullet.** design.md §5 lists "camera-model-aware cropping (later)" as a low-priority upgrade. The survey makes it a *load-bearing universal*: it is the survey's commonality #3 ("crops are the universal currency between localization and 2D estimation"), and **4 of 9 papers require fisheye→virtual-pinhole rewarp** (UmeTrack, EgoExo-Hands, AssemblyHands-ego) or distortion-aware undistort-with-keypoints (Kineo). The current `ops.crops` (square box + pad only) cannot express these. This is an amendment because the design treats crop as ad-hoc consumer glue folded into `TopDownPose2d`, whereas the survey shows it is a distinct, reusable, camera-aware transform that also emits a *virtual CameraModel* the 3D stage consumes.

2. **A latent/feature-encoder variant of the 2D role is missing.** design.md's `TopDownPose2d` and `TopDownDenseLandmarks2d` both emit explicit points. But **UmeTrack (CNN encoder → latent `z_i^I`) and AssemblyHands MVExoNet (EfficientNet feature maps)** never emit keypoints — they emit per-view image features that feed a *learnable* 3D fusion. This is not covered by any current role. It is an amendment (add `TopDownFeatureEncoder2d` as a sibling role, or explicitly declare it out-of-scope as an end-to-end-net exception — see Risks §5).

3. **The `identity` (cross-view/temporal association) stage needs an explicit home decision.** design.md mentions `IdentityEncoder` (CLIP embeddings) and says epipolar/Hungarian association "stays in consumers," but never names association as a pipeline stage. The survey elevates it to a canonical stage present in 4 papers with genuinely different realizations (MAMMA epipolar+Hungarian+cycle-consistency, EPFL depth-3D-merge+reproject-select, AssemblyHands body-fixed hand-id, plus the L/R-by-rig degenerate case). The role split is right (`IdentityEncoder` = network, association = glue) but design.md should say so explicitly and note that `BoxDetections.track_ids` is the boundary that carries the *result*.

4. **`verify` (render-back / consistency gate) is a real recurring stage the design omits entirely.** 4 of 9 papers have it (AssemblyX differentiable silhouette→L_mask, HO-Cap render-to-all-views + 2D export, EPFL fit-vs-lifted discard gate, EgoExo-Hands terminal overlay). It is pure consumer glue (no posekit network), but the design should acknowledge it as a named consumer stage so the boundary types (`DenseLandmarks2d`/`Keypoints2d`/masks) are known to flow *backwards* into it.

**Net:** the network-role set posekit *owns* is correct and complete for 7 of 9 papers. The amendments are about (a) promoting `crop` to camera-aware first-class, (b) admitting the feature-encoder exception, and (c)/(d) naming two consumer stages the design under-specified.

### (c) The universal boundary datatype (the center of gravity)

`posekit/predictions.py`, all `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`, GPU-resident torch tensors:

- **`BoxDetections`** — `xyxy`, `scores`, `frame_indices` + optional `masks`, `track_ids`. The single unifying type for detector / tracker / segmenter output. **This is how `detect`, `identity`(result), and `feedback`(propagated masks) all communicate.**
- **`Keypoints2d`** — `xy`, mandatory `scores` (confidence), `frame_indices`, `skeleton: KeypointSkeleton` + optional `uncertainty`. **The one datatype the whole survey rotates around.** The `pose2d` boundary and the input to `lift3d`/`calibrate`/`verify`.
- **`DenseLandmarks2d`** — `xy`, `log_variance`, `visibility`, `contact`, `floor_contact` (anonymous surface points). The `pose2d` boundary for MammaNet-style dense nets.
- **`Keypoints3d`** — `xy`, `z_root_relative`, `scores`, `skeleton`, `root_indices` + optional `xyz_camera`. The `lift3d`/single-view-3D boundary (container exists, producer GAP).
- **`ParametricPose3d`** (NEW, Phase 4) — model params (SMPL-X β/θ/trans; MANO θ; 26-DOF hand θ) + joints3d + verts + weak-persp cam. The `fit` boundary when a *network* regresses the fit (UmeTrack, AssemblyHands-SVEgoNet, WiLoR).
- **`CameraModel`** (simplecv) — travels *beside* every boundary type from `capture` onward; the `crop` stage forks it into a *virtual* pinhole camera.
- **`SegmentationPrompts`** — prompt payload into segmenters.
- **`KeypointSkeleton` + `SKELETONS` registry** — the named-convention half of the boundary. GAPs: halpe-26, h36m-17, body-25, sapiens-308, mamma-512, and all format-projection tables.

## 3. PER-PAPER REBUILD

Notation: `Role(model)` = posekit-owned; `glue[...]` = consumer; `[external]` = out-of-posekit net; `⟳` = feedback edge.

1. **MEgATrack** = `PersonDetector(DetNet)` → `ops.crops[square+pad, R-mirror, +projected-kpt channel]` → `TopDownPose2d(KeyNet: 2D heatmaps + 1D rel-dist head)` → glue[no explicit lift; 4-view reproj energy] → glue[fit: 26-DOF template LM, E_2D+E_dist+E_temporal; per-user scale φ in calibrate] ⟳ glue[pose extrapolation θ̂=2θ_{t-1}−θ_{t-2} → detection boxes + KeyNet augmentation]. *(1D rel-dist head is a KeyNet-specific output — needs a custom prediction field; feedback loop is pure consumer.)*

2. **UmeTrack** = *(no detector; ROI from loop)* → `ops.crops[fisheye→virtual-pinhole, NEW]` → **`TopDownFeatureEncoder2d(ResNet)`** *(NEW role — emits latent z_i^I, not keypoints)* → **learnable lift** glue/`[external]`[FTL + 1×1-conv multi-view fusion] → glue[calibrate: Regressor-U hand-scale] → glue[fit: Regressor-K + SVD root + FK+LBS] ⟳ glue[RNN hidden state + tracked-pose→ROI/intrinsics]. **← the hardest fit for the abstraction; see Risk §5.**

3. **Kineo** = `PersonDetector`-via-pose-adapter *(full-frame, no box net)* / `VideoSegmenter(SAM2)`[re-ID glue, assumed given] → `ops.crops[undistort images+keypoints via solved Brown-Conrady, NEW]` → `TopDownPose2d(NLF / RTMPose / DWPose — explicitly swappable)` → glue[weighted-DLT + consensus] → **glue[calibrate: FULL calibration-free block — essential-graph→MST→3-pass BA→metric scale]** ⟳ glue[audio-MFCC sync, feed-forward only]. *(The one paper whose center of mass is `calibrate` — all consumer glue; posekit contributes only the swappable `TopDownPose2d` + camera-aware undistort.)*

4. **EPFL-Smart-Kitchen** = `PersonDetector`-via-pose-adapter *(full-frame RTMPose)* + glue[identity: Kinect-depth 3D-merge → reproject-to-select] → `TopDownPose2d(RTMPose-x body + RTMW-x hands)` → glue[weighted-SVD triangulation, conf<0.1 dropped] → glue[fit: EasyMocap SMPL+MANO, 3D+2D-reproj+temporal-smooth+ego-hand loss] → **glue[verify: fit-vs-lifted-pose discard gate]** ⟳ glue[temporal-smoothing loss, feed-forward]. *(multi-modal: Kinect depth + HoloLens ego + IMU are consumer fusion inputs, not posekit roles.)*

## 5. RISKS — where the abstraction could be wrong

1. **Learnable multi-view fusion breaks the clean network/glue split (highest risk).** The abstraction's load-bearing assumption is "networks = detect/segment/pose2d; the geometry tail (lift3d/fit) = consumer glue." **UmeTrack and AssemblyHands MVExoNet violate this**: their 3D lift is *inside a differentiable network* (FTL + learnable triangulation; softmax feature-volume + V2V-PoseNet). There is no clean `pose2d → Keypoints2d → glue[triangulate]` boundary — the boundary type between their `pose2d` and `lift3d` is an opaque feature tensor, not `Keypoints2d`. If posekit tries to own these as `TopDownFeatureEncoder2d + learnable-fusion`, the "fusion" is a *network* that the design says should be glue — contradiction. **Mitigation:** treat end-to-end learned-fusion multi-view nets as a declared exception (they enter posekit as a single opaque role or stay fully external), and keep the `Keypoints2d`-centered abstraction for the 7/9 modular pipelines it fits. Do not force them through the boundary type.

2. **Query-based single-stage models cannot consume external boxes (design already flags; survey doesn't add one, but the risk stands).** RF-DETR/ED-Pose condition keypoints on internal query embeddings, so `InstancePose2d` genuinely *cannot* be decomposed into `PersonDetector ∘ TopDownPose2d`. If a consumer assumes it can always inject its own detector, that assumption fails for this whole model class. **Mitigation:** the design's asymmetric-adapter rule (`InstancePose2d → PersonDetector` trivial, reverse impossible) is correct — enforce it in the type system, never expose a `boxes=` argument on `InstancePose2d`.

3. **Masks-as-input vs masks-as-target vs no-masks is a three-way fork the single `BoxDetections.masks` field hides.** MAMMA/HO-Cap feed masks *into* the estimator (`TopDownDenseLandmarks2d` requires them, raising if `None`); AssemblyX uses masks only as a *fit target* (never reaches the estimator); the rest use none. A naive consumer wiring a `PromptableSegmenter` before a `TopDownPose2d` might assume masks always flow forward into pose — but for AssemblyX they flow *backward* into `verify`. **Mitigation:** the role signatures already encode this (only `TopDownDenseLandmarks2d` takes masked detections; `verify` is consumer-side) — but document that masks have three distinct dataflow roles so the boundary type isn't over-interpreted.

4. **Confidence-less estimators (MediaPipe / HO-Cap) violate the "scores mandatory" invariant.** `Keypoints2d.scores` is mandatory, but MediaPipe emits none — HO-Cap manufactures a per-joint weight from reprojection error *after* triangulation. A posekit MediaPipe adapter would have to synthesize placeholder scores (all-1.0), which is a lie the downstream weighted-DLT would trust. **Mitigation:** either forbid confidence-less models as `TopDownPose2d` impls, or add an explicit `scores_are_synthetic: bool` marker so consumers know to recover real weights downstream. Do not silently fill 1.0.

5. **The `crop` stage emitting a virtual `CameraModel` couples posekit to simplecv's camera model more tightly than the design's "posekit is network-only" stance implies.** Camera-aware crop *must* return corrected intrinsics/extrinsics for `lift3d` to be correct, which means `posekit.ops.crops` now depends on and produces `CameraModel` — a geometry object the design otherwise keeps in simplecv. **Mitigation:** accept the dependency (simplecv is already a posekit dep and owns `Fisheye62Parameters`); keep the *triangulation* that consumes the virtual camera in the consumer, so posekit produces the corrected camera but never fuses with it. The line stays "posekit warps and re-parameterizes cameras; consumers triangulate with them."
